evidence: the-managed-user-becomes-root-with-sudo: user_sudoer.pp:10-11 appends sudo to the group list on non-RedHat (Ubuntu node); line 18 creates p8testuser from the params fixture whose hash is the test password, so sudo -S with it yields uid 0, a wrong password and nobody (not in sudo) are refused; the effect reads the recorded answers, not the action's output

the-agent-run-leaves-the-unmanaged-account-alone: users_sudoers.pp:15-18 filters p8testuser2 (in unmanaged_users) out before create_resources, so the catalog has no user_sudoer for it and an agent run must leave a hand-made p8testuser2 (passwd line, shadow digest, groups) unchanged, not in sudo, with no authorized_keys; mutates truthfully declares nothing (action is true)

managed-user-is-a-sudoer: users_sudoers.pp:18 create_resources of the filtered hash declares user_sudoer p8testuser with myname 'P8 Test User' and an empty mygrouplist, so passwd comment is 'P8 Test User' and groups are its own group plus sudo (user_sudoer.pp:11)

purpose covered: The define's own job is filter + create_resources (users_sudoers.pp:15,18): the checks prove a managed entry becomes a working sudoer (groups, sudo to root with its password; wrong password and non-member refused), an unmanaged entry is not created, and a hand-made account of the unmanaged name survives an agent run untouched.
